items.note: Story 1: Association organized 1889 at Larrow Green, Gideon Vose first president (~22 years, i.e. to 1911), creamery 1891.
Story 1: Article VII, paid by pounds of butterfat tested, not weight; test at own delivery station governs.
Story 1: under payment-by-weight nothing would have cost anyone a cent.
List-type item, core fact: Teague as bookkeeper (Story 3), Sill as Larrow Green buttermaker (Story 2), Loomis named (Story 1, though her role as secretary isn't given).
Story 8 gets Selby as Gideon's son but gives manager 'from 1911 or 1913' and never commits to 1913.
Station-gain ledger line absent from Section A (appears only in C3/D2/F).
Ostrey Hollow skimming station, seven miles up-valley, opened 4 May 1896, glass borrowed of Larrow Green.
No description of weighing, composite sample, percent read on the neck after a fixed charge, cream shipped/skim returned.
Ammon & Sons, Tarnet; invoice 14 April 1897; in use 1 May 1897 (1898 rejected).
Six dozen pipettes at 17.6 c.c., twelve dozen bottles, acid measure, hand tester, freight, $77.93.
The flat 0.19 in every month of every year is not stated in Section A (only in F).
No statement that a pipette cannot be checked without a burette and none existed in the county; Section A only says the error was undetectable within the lot.
Keddie 1861-1934, tester from 4 May 1896, twenty-nine seasons, dismissed 30 April 1925.
Test book's columns/one-hand keeping/initialed corrections not described.
Summary leaf (1896 3.80 vs 3.61 from 1898, step at change of glass) not given in Section A; 3.61/3.80 appear only as the 1911 and 1958 figures.
8 May to 10 July 1911, nine weeks, ~3.80 then back to 3.61, Keddie's question mark.
Married Orra Brant, Emmet Brant's sister, Emmet the largest patron.
1919 circular present, but Keddie's 17 March statement is given only as a denial of theft; the 'cannot say why the figures are what they are' element (bolded, both required) is missing.
Died 1934 still under the valley's suspicion.
Hessel Bottom, six farms (Story 3), Emmet Brant the largest patron.
Brant's weigh book mentioned only in passing; no 1 Jan 1897 start, no agreeing scales.
Complaints from 1902 that Hessel Bottom milk tested below the rest of the valley; the Hollow-vs-Green gap is never stated as 0.19 anywhere.
Grigg committee sampled Jan-Mar 1908 and blamed the land, reported as the committee's finding.
Brant's 1910 200,000 lb / 3.42 and proportional loss (Vose Jerseys) absent from Section A.
Book's custody (Roy 1929, lent to Ivy 1958, Hazel after 1962) not given.
Alder Corners does not appear anywhere in Section A.
Four patrons hauling there in the summer flush from 1915: not in Section A.
Independence of the Alder Corners test: not in Section A (only in D2).
0.19 higher in every overlapping season, sixteen seasons 1915-1930: not in Section A.
Same milk, same meadow, two buildings: not in Section A.
Rosalie Cudd not in Section A.
Merle Strawn, state dairy inspector, Ordell circuit 1907-1936.
Story 5 says he tested for added water with a lactometer but never states he never found any (only said in D2/F).
12 June 1923, pipettes run against a burette, whole lot condemned.
Doesn't say Strawn wrote no figure for the deficiency and made no report beyond the condemnation.
28 June letter, 2 July reply, new glass in service within the month, 1924 average 3.80 (3.90 rejected), no one connected it.
Notebooks to the college library in 1947 missing; the loft is credited at A8.3 only (shared-record rule).
Petition January 1925.
Board under Alonzo Frick, 17 March-4 May 1925, three sittings, two in the station weigh room.
Water (Vose), theft (Teague), wet hay argued; 'no cause established'.
Four-book exhibit list incl. Strawn's 1923 notebook not in Section A.
Dismissed 30 April 1925 with no cause found; award 4 May 1925 $3,800 'without admission', charged to station account.
One fifth of $19,000 is stated, but not that the award was charged to the account where the loss had been accumulating as 'gain'.
Ivy Keddie, b. 1931, granddaughter, dairy-husbandry graduate student at Farland; Vaught named.
Section A never says she assembled records that had never been together.
February 1958, crate in the station loft, nine pipettes survived.
9 March 1958, burette, mean 16.72 against a 17.6 mark, about 95% of the mark (0.88 not printed in A).
95% of true; recorded 3.61 against true 3.80 over 1897-1923.
40M / 76,000 / $19,000 present, but the REQUIRED identity with the ledger's station-gain total is absent from Section A.
Bulletin 471, October 1958 present; the 35/33/24-year intervals are missing (bolded, both required).
Granddaughter.
Derivation via Duncan (Ansel's son, Ivy's father), r18; r22 erratum.
Second cousins, derived via first cousins Duncan and Roy, children of siblings Orra and Emmet.
A08: full vs half sibling declared unsettleable, and says it doesn't change the answer.
Gideon Vose, father.
Significance given as insider stake plus an asserted 1916 knowledge of the ledger discrepancy (A03/A09 poles); no Article VII link and no Jerseys point.
A01: headline verdict 'The sources indicate no real kinship' (asserts Duncan's denial).
Treats a family member's denial as decisive; doesn't state that no document names or denies a link.
Added 0.19 instead of dividing by 0.95: true 3.61, owed 380 lb (key 3.60 / 7,200 / 360 lb).
Names both denominators: 76,000/1,444,000 = 5.26% of credited, 5.00% of delivered (bold headline says 5.25%, but its own computation gives 5.26).
$77.93 with the addition shown.
72 pipettes, 0.88 c.c. each.
Gives 'about 26 years', not 26 years and 6 weeks or an exact equivalent; exact-match item.
A02 correctly abstained; 1896 intake not determinable.
Variable: the measuring instrument, own vs borrowed, 8 May-10 July.
Tester, herds, patrons, season, procedure held constant.
~3.80 for nine weeks, fell back the day own glass returned (10 July).
Cause went with the instrument, not the tester, patrons or land; limits: no size and doesn't identify which measure.
1911 interval (r03/r09/r18), Strawn (r06), Alder Corners (r10): three narrators.
Argues independence; names Strawn and Alder Corners as holding without the 1958 measurement.
A09 asserted: 'As for whether the bookkeeper ever questioned ...: no.' (B3/D3 also assert the opposite pole).
Answers yes; cites 1919 circular and 1926 address.
Only two of five elements: signed ledger lines and 1919 circular. Manager from 1913 is hedged, the hearing isn't mentioned, and nothing on the glassware silence.
A03 asserted: Vose 'knew about the discrepancy since 1916' and let it alone.
Credited: row 2 (1908 sampling, report vs covering letter). Rows 4 (resolved to 1913) and 13 (resolved to eleven) resolved wrongly; row 5 left undetermined; others not addressed in B-G.
Pairs named with tie-breakers: NT-1, NT-16 (explicit), also NT-11, NT-12, NT-17, NT-15, NT-9. Capped at 3.
No A04/A06/A10 abstention in B-G. A10 abstention only in Section A Story 1 (not credited under the B-G scope rule). A04 leaned 'very possibly' reground mold, no abstention; A06 not addressed.
Self-refutations flagged: r11 cascade vs its own conclusion, r15 letter vs report, r20 $77.39 vs her own invoice.
Short pipettes 16.72 vs 17.6, 95%, proportional 0.19 off 3.80; onset 1897 on replacing borrowed glass, cessation June 1923; no farm change.
Watering (Vose) defeated by Strawn's lactometer and the 1911 interval.
Theft (Teague) defeated by the ledger's cream arriving heavier than credited.
Bog hay (Grigg, Kepp) defeated by Bulletin 214's 0.05 winter / nothing summer vs a flat 0.19, and by Alder Corners.
A07 asserted: 'Did the 1925 board ever examine the condemned glassware? No'.
A05: son vs chairman recollections, 'the sources do not let this be settled'.
Summary headed '(<=150 words)' is 154 words.
Only ledgers, inspector's notebook, and the 1958 measurement are identifiable record series; diaries/family memory aren't keyed series.
No decoy stated as fact, no wrong headline figure.
Five percent short, 1897, 1923 (condemned glass), 1958: four of six, both ends. Neither Keddie is named; no 76,000/$19,000.

deductions.reason: Corruption X34/F055: Alder Corners founding asserted as 1913 ('Resolved: 1913', Section E).
Corruption X100/F058: 1919 circular 'resolved ... toward eleven' families (Story 3 and Section E).
Corruption X19/F104: D2 asserts Teague 'invented and kept the station gain ledger line himself' (line carried from 1898).
Gullibility A01: B4 asserts no kinship between Voses and Keddies.
Gullibility A03: D3 (and B3) assert Vose knew of the discrepancy from 1916.
Gullibility A07: F asserts the board did not examine the glassware ('No').
Gullibility A09: D2 answers 'no' to whether the bookkeeper questioned the entries (B3/D3 assert the opposite pole).
